REEL

THE CAFÉ RACER

How Coffee Gave Birth to Motorcycle Culture

DOING THE TON

0:00 / 0:00

Narration

Nineteen fifties London. A jukebox starts playing. Young men sprint to their motorcycles and race into the night. The goal? Hit a hundred miles per hour and return before the song ends. They called it doing the ton. They stripped their bikes bare. Removed mudguards, lowered the handlebars, cut the exhausts short. These were the Ton-Up Boys of the Ace Cafe. And they built a culture that changed motorcycling forever.
